public_rationale: OpenAI announced GPT-4.1 on April 14, two weeks before the post, with lower prices than GPT-4o. That is a direct counterexample to the claim that its latest models only become more expensive. GPT-4.5 was indeed more expensive than GPT-4o, but that example does not establish the claimed general trend.
limitations: The comparison concerns API customer prices, not OpenAI's total spending or cost per completed task.
The cited 26% reduction uses OpenAI's median query mix; individual workloads can differ.

our_interpretation: The adjacent per-token figures identify customer API prices as the ordinary measure of expensive.

criteria.support_condition: Published API prices show that successive comparable recent OpenAI models consistently became more expensive.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Before the post, OpenAI released a comparable newer model at lower API prices than its predecessor or the existing model it was replacing.
